title.en: 이다 vs 아니다 and 있다 vs 없다

title.ko: 의문사: 누구 · 언제 · 어디 · 무엇 · 왜
몸 · 아플 때 쓰는 말 · 병원
부정과 시제: 안 · 못 · 과거 · 미래

cards.en: How do you do? (very formal, first meeting)
Please take care of me. / I look forward to working with you.
Welcome. (said to someone who comes in)

quiz.q: You meet your new boss for the first time. What is the best thing to say?
quiz.why: 처음 뵙겠습니다 is the formal way to greet someone you meet for the first time.

quiz.q: A customer walks into your shop. What do you say?
quiz.why: 어서 오세요 means welcome. The shop says it to the person who comes in.

quiz.q: 저는 일본에서 왔어요 means:
quiz.why: -에서 왔어요 means came from. 일본에서 = from Japan.

quiz.q: Which question asks about someone's nationality?
quiz.why: 어느 나라 사람이에요? literally asks which country person you are.

quiz.q: Before bed, you say good night to your grandmother.
quiz.why: 안녕히 주무세요 is the respectful form of good night for an older person.

fill.en: Nice to meet you.
I came from the USA.
What is your name?
Please take care of me.
Welcome.

quiz.q: Which letter makes the 'm' sound in Korean?
quiz.why: ㅁ (미음) represents the m sound, as in 모자 (hat).

quiz.q: Which of the following is a horizontal vowel written below the consonant?
quiz.why: ㅗ is a horizontal vowel and is positioned directly underneath the initial consonant, like in 고.

quiz.q: When ㅇ is used at the beginning of a syllable block (like in 오), what sound does it make?
opts: It is silent and serves as a placeholder.
quiz.why: At the beginning of a syllable, ㅇ has no sound and simply holds the space for the vowel.

quiz.q: What syllable is formed by combining the consonant ㄱ and the vowel ㅏ?
quiz.why: ㄱ (g/k) plus vertical vowel ㅏ (a) forms the syllable block 가 (ga).

quiz.q: What is the official Korean name for the consonant letter ㄴ?
quiz.why: The consonant ㄴ is officially called 니은 (nieun).

fill.en: The name of consonant ㄱ is giyeok.

fill.q: 자음 ㅂ과 모음 ㅏ가 만나면 ___가 됩니다.
fill.en: When consonant ㅂ and vowel ㅏ meet, it becomes ba.
The first syllable of the word haneul (sky) is ha.
The official name of the Hangul consonant ㄴ is nieun.

fill.q: 자음 ㅅ과 모음 ㅗ를 결합하면 ___가 됩니다.
fill.en: Combining consonant ㅅ and vowel ㅗ creates so.

cards.en: final consonant (batchim at the bottom of a block)
liaison (carrying a batchim over to a following vowel)

quiz.q: How many representative batchim sounds exist when final consonants are pronounced in isolation?
quiz.why: All Korean final consonants collapse into one of 7 representative sounds: [ㄱ ㄴ ㄷ ㄹ ㅁ ㅂ ㅇ].

quiz.q: What representative sound does the final consonant in 옷 (clothes) make when spoken alone?
quiz.why: The letter ㅅ simplifies to the representative stop sound [ㄷ] at the end of a syllable.

quiz.q: According to the liaison rule (연음), how is the phrase 부엌에 pronounced?
quiz.why: The final consonant ㅋ moves into the silent ㅇ of 에, so 부엌에 is read [부어케].

quiz.q: Which of the following words ends with the [ㅂ] representative sound when spoken alone?
quiz.why: 밥 ends with ㅂ, which is pronounced as the representative bilabial stop [ㅂ].

quiz.q: How is the phrase 집에 (to home) pronounced in natural spoken Korean?
quiz.why: Due to liaison, the final ㅂ carries over into the following vowel 에, producing [지베].

fill.en: Reading practice: the sound of 꽃이 is [kkochi].
The sound of 밖에 is [bakke].
The representative batchim sound of the word ip (leaf) is [ㅂ].

fill.q: 꽃 한 송이를 발음할 때 받침 소리는 [___]으로 바뀝니다.
fill.en: When pronouncing a flower (꽃), the final consonant changes to [ㄷ].
The sound of 닫는 is [danneun].

cards.en: do not have / there is no

quiz.q: Which ending should you attach to a noun ending in a vowel to say 'is' (e.g., 의사)?
quiz.why: Nouns ending in a vowel attach -예요 without a particle (의사예요).

quiz.q: How do you say 'I am not a student' in polite Korean?
quiz.why: To negate identity, attach 이/가 아니에요 to the noun: 학생이 아니에요.

quiz.q: Which sentence correctly expresses 'I have an umbrella'?
quiz.why: Possession of an object uses Noun + 이/가 있어요: 우산이 있어요.

quiz.q: What particle is used before 아니에요, 있어요, and 없어요?
quiz.why: 아니에요, 있어요, and 없어요 all require the subject particle 이/가 on the preceding noun.

quiz.q: What does 지갑에 돈이 없어요 mean?
opts: I have no money in my wallet.
There is money in the wallet.
quiz.why: 돈이 없어요 means there is no money / I do not have money.

fill.en: My job is an office worker.
I am not a singer.
There is a key in my pocket right now.
I am thirsty, but there is no water to drink.
The person over there is a kind nurse.

cards.en: that over there (modifier far from both)

quiz.q: Which word would you use to refer to a pen sitting right beside the listener?
quiz.why: 그 refers to items close to the listener or already mentioned in conversation.

quiz.q: What is the common spoken contraction of 이것이 (this thing as subject)?
quiz.why: 이것이 contracts to 이게 in natural everyday speech.

quiz.q: You want to say 'Please sit here' pointing to a chair next to you. Which word means 'here'?
quiz.why: 여기 means 'here' (the place near the speaker).

quiz.q: When both you and your friend are looking at a distant building across the river, which word should you use?
quiz.why: 저 is used for people or objects visible but distant from both speaker and listener.

quiz.q: How do native speakers naturally say 'What is that (near you)?' in spoken Korean?
quiz.why: 그게 (short for 그것이) refers to an item near the listener.

fill.q: 제 손에 들고 있는 ___ 사과는 정말 달아요.
fill.en: This apple that I am holding in my hand is really sweet.

fill.q: 책상 위에 놓인 ___ 모자는 누구 거예요?
fill.en: Whose is that hat on the desk?

fill.q: 멀리 보이는 ___ 비행기가 참 높이 날고 있어요.
fill.en: That airplane visible far away is flying very high.

fill.q: 처음 오셨으면 편한 자리에 앉아 ___서 기다려 주세요.
fill.en: If it is your first time here, please sit in a comfortable seat and wait here.

fill.q: 식당 종업원을 부를 때 공손하게 '___요!'라고 말해요.
fill.en: When calling a restaurant server, we politely say 'Excuse me (over there)!'

cards.en: location particle where action happens (at / in)

quiz.q: Which object particle attaches to a noun ending in a consonant, such as 책 (book)?
quiz.why: Nouns ending in a batchim take 을 as the direct object particle (책을).

quiz.q: Which sentence correctly describes studying inside the library?
quiz.why: Use 에서 for the location where an active event (like studying) takes place.

quiz.q: You are traveling to school by subway. Which particle means 'by' (transportation)?
quiz.why: Nouns ending in ㄹ take 로 directly without inserting 으: 지하철 + 로 = 지하철로.

quiz.q: How do you say 'I eat bread and milk' using the formal connecting particle 과/와?
quiz.why: 빵 ends in batchim ㅇ, so it takes 과: 빵과 우유.

quiz.q: Which particle specifies an exact meeting time, such as 'at 3 o'clock'?
quiz.why: Specific time points take the static particle 에 (3시에 만나요).

fill.en: My younger sibling washes fresh apples every morning.
I drank warm green tea for breakfast.

fill.q: 내일 오후 두 시___ 교실에서 회의가 시작돼요.
fill.en: The meeting starts at 2 PM tomorrow in the classroom.
Our family eats dinner in the living room.

fill.q: 부산까지 빠른 기차___ 이동하면 두 시간 걸려요.
fill.en: If you travel by fast train to Busan, it takes two hours.

quiz.q: When 누구 (who) is combined with the subject particle 가, how is it correctly written?
quiz.why: When 누구 acts as the subject with particle 가, it must always contract to 누가.

quiz.q: Which question word asks about location ('where')?
quiz.why: 어디 specifically asks about places or locations.

quiz.q: Which word is used to ask for the price of an item in Korean (e.g., 'How much is this?')?
quiz.why: 얼마 is used to ask about monetary prices: 이거 얼마예요? (How much is this?).

quiz.q: Which question asks 'What time is it right now?' using counter word 시 (o'clock)?
quiz.why: 몇 is used directly before counter nouns: 지금 몇 시예요? (What time is it now?).

quiz.q: How do you ask someone 'Why are you learning Korean?'
quiz.why: 왜 asks for the reason or purpose behind an action ('Why').

fill.en: Where is the hometown of the newly transferred student?
When is the starting time for tomorrow's birthday party?
What do you want to eat for lunch today?

fill.q: 방과 후에 운동장에서 축구를 한 사람은 ___예요?
fill.en: Who is the person who played soccer on the field after school?
How long does it take walking from the subway station to the office?
